title: The staff and the shining hand
word: The staff and the shining hand
hookLine: his staff becomes a snake and his hand comes out white and shining: two signs
last: YOU ARE IN A SACRED VALLEY.

cards: Look down at your hands. What's in them? A phone, probably.
A coffee. A steering wheel, hopefully not. It's easy to stop noticing what you carry.
Musa is still standing barefoot in the sacred valley. He's just been told who God is, and that he's been chosen. The next thing he hears isn't a thunderclap or a list of orders.
It's a question, almost casual, the kind a friend asks, about the thing in his hand.

teach.h: WHAT IS THAT IN THY RIGHT HAND?
teach.b: Surah Ta-Ha. In Pickthall's old translation: "And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses?" Of course Allah knows what it is.
So why ask? Some commentators say it was to make Musa look closely at something ordinary, so he'd know exactly what it was before it changed. And Musa answers at length.

teach.h: MY STAFF: I LEAN ON IT.
teach.b: It's my staff. I lean on it. I knock leaves down with it for my sheep.
And I have other uses for it too. Some commentators smile at that long answer: a man just spoken to by his Lord, who doesn't want the conversation to end.

teach.h: A SNAKE, THEN A STAFF AGAIN.
teach.b: Then: throw it down. He does, and it's a snake, moving fast. Take it, and don't be afraid; We'll return it to how it was.
Then the second sign: put your hand under your arm, and it will come out white, without any harm. The Qur'an adds that phrase, and commentators read it as ruling out illness: light, not sickness.

teach.h: TWO SIGNS, FROM WHAT HE HAD.
teach.b: Two signs, both from what he already has. A shepherd's stick. His own hand.
Nothing brought down from the sky. The ordinary thing, looked at properly, turns out to be enough for the mission. And that's the week.
A mother's hands letting go of a chest. A queen's arms. A sister who spoke up.
A blow Musa regretted. Water at a well. A fire on a mountain.
And now a staff. Seven days, and most of the turning points were in someone's hands.

how: Muslims count the staff and the shining hand among the signs, ayat, given to Musa, and the story is often told to show how Allah works through ordinary things.

games.q: what does “the staff and the shining hand” mean?
o: two signs made from what Musa already had
two weapons Musa used against Pharaoh's army
two magic tricks Musa learned in Egypt

games.q: you're Musa, barefoot in the sacred valley. a voice asks: what is that in your right hand? what do you say?
o: it's my staff. I lean on it, and I have other uses for it.
games.why: he answers at length, and some commentators say it's because he didn't want the conversation to end. then: throw it down.

practice: Look at what's in your hand, the phone or the cup, or your empty hand: turn it over, see the lines, the knuckles, the small scar you forgot you had.
Then ask the question the way it was asked in the valley, what is this, and answer honestly, at length if you like, like Musa: what does it do for you, and what else could it be used for?
If you pray, you can offer what's in your hand to Allah.

orig.note: Arabic: staff, the shepherd's stick Musa leaned on, from Qur'an 20:18.

carryVoice: Your line: what's in your right hand? Usually, something ordinary. A week with Musa, done.
